# Database {#sec-db}

```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
```

The **source of truth** for the Marine Sensitivity Toolkit is DuckDB — a columnar, embedded analytic database. It is fast enough to answer live per-cell queries while remaining a single-file artifact that can be copied, versioned and served read-only to many processes at once.

The pipeline writes a working database (`sdm.duckdb`) on the machine that runs it; a **release** is the published, immutable form of that database's tables. Since the marine-atlas release format, each version is published as **partitioned Parquet on S3** under `marine-atlas/{ver}/tables/`, and serving reads it through a tiny view-only DuckDB (`serve.duckdb`, kilobytes) whose tables are *views* over those files — never a multi-gigabyte copy.

Everything below is read from the release this build documents (**`r doc_ver()`**), so the tables, columns and row counts are those of that version rather than of whichever version happened to be current when the page was written.

::: {.callout-note}
**Why DuckDB and not PostgreSQL?** Earlier versions of the stack used PostgreSQL + PostGIS as the primary store. As the analysis stabilized around a fixed 0.05° cell grid and a small set of zone layers, live geometry operations and concurrent writes stopped being needed — only fast analytic reads. DuckDB scans tens of millions of rows in well under a second with no separate server process. PostGIS is no longer part of the serving path (see @sec-server).
:::

## Table and column naming conventions

- Table names are singular and lower case.
- Unique identifier columns are suffixed with:
  - `*_id` for unique integer keys (stable across rebuilds);
  - `*_key` for unique string keys (human-readable and stable across releases);
  - `*_seq` for auto-incrementing sequence integer keys (internal join keys, **not** stable across rebuilds).
- Column names are singular and use `snake_case`.
- Foreign keys use the singular form of the referenced table, followed by the primary-key suffix (`_id`, `_key`, or `_seq`).

::: {.callout-important}
## `value` is a reserved word in DuckDB

Cell values are stored in a column named **`val`**, not `value`. The serving views expose `val AS value` for backward compatibility with callers written against the older schema.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-db-tables
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Tables published by ", doc_ver(), ", with row counts read from the release itself.")

purposes <- c(
  cell        = "Grid cells of the study area, with environmental covariates and membership flags.",
  taxon       = "One row per taxon: identity, category, extinction risk and validity flags.",
  model       = "Registry of every distribution model, keyed by the stable model identifier.",
  model_asset = "Crosswalk from a model to its published raster/vector assets.",
  taxon_model = "Which models fed which taxon — the taxon to model relation.",
  listing     = "US federal listing lookup (ESA status, MMPA and MBTA protection).",
  dataset     = "Source datasets, with citations, vintages and whether each fed the scores.",
  metric      = "Metric registry: key and description for each scored quantity.",
  cell_metric = "Per-cell score for each metric — the surface the maps draw.",
  zone        = "Zone registry keyed by source table, field and value, so every spatial unit shares one schema.",
  zone_cell   = "Zone membership: which cells belong to which zone.",
  zone_metric = "Pre-aggregated per-zone score for each metric — what drives the choropleth.",
  zone_taxon  = "Per-zone species list with each species' contribution to the zone score.",
  native_asset = "Per-release pointers from each model to its distribution files (COGs, PMTiles) in the asset store (@sec-asset-store); the Atlas reads it to draw each input.")

tbls <- doc_tables()
rows <- vapply(tbls, function(t) tryCatch(doc_nrow(t), error = function(e) NA_real_), numeric(1))

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Table   = paste0("`", tbls, "`"),
    Rows    = ifelse(is.na(rows), "—", formatC(rows, format = "d", big.mark = ",")),
    Purpose = ifelse(tbls %in% names(purposes), purposes[tbls], ""),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL),
  align = c("l", "r", "l"))
```

```{r}
#| label: db-absent
#| output: asis

# What this release does NOT publish is as informative as what it does — and
# saying so is what keeps a v1 page from implying it had tables it never had.
absent <- setdiff(names(purposes), tbls)
if (length(absent)) cat(
  "::: {.callout-note}\n## Not published by ", doc_ver(), "\n\n",
  paste0("`", absent, "`", collapse = ", "),
  ". Sections that depend on these are omitted from this build rather than described from another release.\n:::\n",
  sep = "")
```

## Schema

The columns of each published table, read from the release:

```{r}
#| label: db-schema
#| output: asis

for (t in tbls) {
  d <- tryCatch(doc_cols(t), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(d)) next
  cat("\n###", paste0("`", t, "`"), "\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(
    data.frame(Column = d$column_name, Type = d$column_type, check.names = FALSE),
    align = c("l", "l")))
  cat("\n")
}
```

## Asset store {#sec-asset-store}

::: {.callout-note}
## Old copies remain until the prune

Every published release (v7, v7b, v8, v9) has pointed only into the store since the **asset-store migration of 2026-10-02**. The copies the v8 and v9 releases carried before it still exist under their release prefixes (`v8/native/`, `v9/native/`) and on the file host, unreferenced, until a prune that follows a soak period. The migration's listing on 2026-10-01 found 145,452 objects (33.08 GB) under those two prefixes, which collapse to 86,421 distinct keys (19.63 GB) in the store, because the two releases carry the same files for most datasets.
:::

**A release owns pointers, never distribution files.** Every cloud-optimized distribution file lives exactly once in an unversioned, content-addressed store, and each release publishes tables whose rows point into it. Nothing ending in `.tif` or `.pmtiles` is written under a release's `{ver}/` prefix. A release prefix holds only its manifest, its tables, its app bundle and its serving files.

There are two stores, both in the project's public S3 bucket:

| Store | Key | Holds |
|:------|:----|:------|
| `cog/` | `cog/{grid_id}/{hash}.tif` | rasters *on an analysis grid*: each input's gridded surface, merged models and score surfaces |
| `native/` | `native/{ds_key}/{hash}.{tif\|pmtiles}` | each source dataset's own resolution original: a raster (`.tif`) or a vector range (`.pmtiles`) |

### The key comes from the content

The `hash` in a key is computed **before** any file is built, from the *source content* of the model plus an **encoding tag**, and never from the bytes of the file or from the release:

- for a gridded surface, the model's `(cell_id, val)` rows;
- for a native raster, the source grid's `(cell_id, val)` rows;
- for a native vector range, the normalized geometry and the attributes that reach the tile;
- the encoding tag names how the file is written (data type, nodata, overviews, tile scheme), so a different encoding of the same content is deliberately a different object.

Two consequences follow. A surface that did not change between releases is found in the store by its key, so it costs neither a build nor an upload; a source dataset such as AquaMaps that is unchanged between releases is registered by a new pointer row and nothing else. And a merged model that equals its only input has the same rows, hence the same key, hence is the same object as that input, with no special case. A re-ingested dataset adds objects only for the models whose content changed; the old objects stay for the releases that still point at them. Scores are always new, because they are per-release tables.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-asset-store
%%| fig-cap: "A release's pointer table refers to objects in the shared stores; the catalog lists every stored object."
flowchart LR
  v8["v8 native_asset"] --> store[("cog/ and native/")]
  v9["v9 native_asset"] --> store
  v10["next release native_asset"] --> store
  cat["assets.parquet"] -.lists.-> store
```

### The catalog and the pointer table

- **`assets.parquet`** at the atlas root (beside the `cog/` and `native/` stores, under the same `marine-atlas/` prefix as the releases) is the catalog, with one row per stored object (store, key, content hash, encoding tag, asset type, grid or dataset key, size, MD5, creation time and the first release that used it). "Is it already stored?" is an anti-join against this file, not a bucket listing.
- **`native_asset`** is the per-release pointer table (@tbl-db-tables). Its `representation = model` rows point into `cog/`, its `native` rows point into `native/`, and a merged model is a row with `ds_key = ms_merge`. Each row carries the content hash and the asset URL; a PMTiles row also carries `source_key`, the model key the tile's features are tagged with, which is how a viewer filters one range out of the archive. Every published release has one in this shape; the earlier releases keep `model_asset` beside it so that old links still resolve.
- An object no release points at is garbage. Nothing is deleted except through a check that joins the catalog against every release's pointer tables.

### Finding a file

The bucket denies anonymous listing, so a file is found through a pointer, not by browsing:

1. read the catalog `assets.parquet` to see what exists and where;
2. read a release's `native_asset` table (`{ver}/tables/native_asset.parquet`) to see which objects that release uses for each model;
3. or ask STAC: the searchable STAC API is built from the pointer table, so each Item's `model` and `native` assets carry the same store URLs, and the static STAC catalog of a release links them once its tree is rebuilt from the pointer table (v7, v7b and v9 today; v8 follows its next rebuild).

### Verify before store

An object is admitted to the store under key *K* only if its decoded pixels equal the rows *K* was computed from. In the migration, a file that failed the check was repainted from the model's current rows and uploaded under its key (2,934 of the raster objects; the rest were copied once their pixels had been verified). A publish applies the same check to every new file before it is uploaded. This keeps what a map draws identical to what the scores used.

See @sec-workflows-asset-store for how a publish writes to the store and what the publish gate checks.

## How the tables feed the serving tier

- **Score rasters** — per-cell scores are published as **Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs**, one per metric × subregion, and the app reads the href and rescale range straight from the release manifest. Earlier releases rendered them by sending SQL to a tile factory per request; that path is retired (see @sec-server).
- **Per-model distributions** — `model_cell` is published partitioned by a dense integer model id, so a tile request reads exactly one partition as a point read rather than scanning the surface.
- **Zone choropleths** — `zone_metric` joined to `zone` gives the per-zone score; the geometry comes from PMTiles published per zone-set **vintage**, and the manifest names the vintage each release used. Only the paint specification changes when the reader switches metric.
- **Per-cell and per-area species lists** — the same rows partitioned by a spatial tile instead (`cell_model`), because a per-cell question against a model-partitioned surface would scan everything.

See @sec-workflows for the notebooks that build each of these tables.
